articles.title: Sicredi chega a Vale de Bonsucesso e fortalece desenvolvimento regional | G1
articles.standfirst: Quinta agência do Sicredi na Região Serrana será inaugurada em 26 de outubro, no 3º Distrito de Teresópolis, e ampliará o atendimento a pessoas, empresas e produtores rurais.
articles.summary: Quinta agência do Sicredi na Região Serrana será inaugurada em 26 de outubro, no 3º Distrito de Teresópolis, e ampliará o atendimento a pessoas, empresas e produtores rurais.
articles.body:
Ilustração do projeto da nova agência do Sicredi no Vale de Bonsucesso, no Terceiro Distrito de Teresópolis. A unidade será inaugurada em 26 de outubro — Foto: Divulgação/Sicredi

O Sicredi dá mais um passo em sua trajetória na Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro com a inauguração, no dia 26 de outubro, da agência do Vale de Bonsucesso, no Terceiro Distrito de Teresópolis. A nova unidade consolida um movimento de expansão que ganhou força em 2026 e eleva para cinco o número de agências da instituição financeira na região.

A ampliação da presença física reforça a estratégia do Sicredi de manter o atendimento humano e próximo como parte central do relacionamento com associados e comunidades. Com a nova estrutura, a instituição amplia o acesso a soluções financeiras para pessoas físicas, empresas e produtores rurais, aproximando serviços e orientação financeira da realidade de quem vive e trabalha na região. O posicionamento de atendimento humano, presença local e soluções para todos esses públicos também integra a estratégia de atuação do Sicredi.

A inauguração representa um importante ciclo de expansão na Região Serrana em 2026. Além da unidade de Vale de Bonsucesso, o Sicredi inaugurou neste ano uma agência em Conquista, no Terceiro Distrito de Nova Friburgo, somando-se às unidades já existentes nos centros de Nova Friburgo, Teresópolis e Petrópolis. Assim, a instituição financeira passa a contar com cinco pontos físicos na região.

Mais do que ampliar sua estrutura, o movimento busca aproximar o atendimento das diferentes realidades encontradas no território. Na Região Serrana e em todo o país, o Sicredi disponibiliza mais de 300 soluções financeiras para diferentes públicos, contemplando necessidades de pessoas, empresas e produtores rurais de todos os portes. Entre elas estão alternativas de crédito, financiamentos, investimentos, consórcios, cartões, poupança e serviços para o cotidiano financeiro.

Presença que acompanha o desenvolvimento da região

A expansão na Região Serrana está conectada ao compromisso do Sicredi com o desenvolvimento dos territórios onde atua. A proximidade permite às equipes conhecer as características econômicas e sociais de cada localidade e construir relacionamentos de longo prazo com moradores, empreendedores e produtores rurais.

Essa atuação ganha importância especial nos terceiros distritos. As duas novas agências inauguradas em 2026 ampliam a presença do Sicredi para além das áreas centrais dos municípios e aproximam o atendimento de comunidades e atividades econômicas locais. A proposta das unidades é atender produtores rurais com maior proximidade, sem deixar de contemplar pessoas físicas e empresas.

Em Vale de Bonsucesso, a atuação do Sicredi começou antes mesmo da inauguração da agência, com atendimentos realizados na localidade. Agora, a nova estrutura fortalece essa presença e oferece um ponto permanente de atendimento e orientação financeira para moradores, empreendedores e produtores rurais.

Para Rafael Martins, diretor de Negócios do Sicredi na Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro, a inauguração representa o fortalecimento de uma presença construída para acompanhar as necessidades e as oportunidades locais.

“Chegar ao Vale de Bonsucesso com uma agência completa representa muito mais do que ampliar nossa estrutura física. É estar mais perto da população, compreender suas necessidades e contribuir para que novos projetos, negócios e oportunidades possam se desenvolver. O Sicredi reinveste nas regiões onde está presente, fazendo com que os recursos movimentados também contribuam para fortalecer a economia e gerar oportunidades em todo o território. Encerramos 2026 com cinco agências na Região Serrana e com a certeza de que estamos construindo uma presença de longo prazo, baseada no relacionamento humano e no compromisso com o desenvolvimento local.”

Cinco agências para estar cada vez mais perto

Com a inauguração de Vale de Bonsucesso, a presença física do Sicredi na Região Serrana passa a ser formada por:

Nova Friburgo: Avenida Alberto Braune, 75, Centro;

Nova Friburgo, 3º Distrito: Avenida Antônio Mario de Azevedo, 2200, Conquista;

Petrópolis: Rua Marechal Deodoro, 50, Centro;

Teresópolis: Avenida Delfim Moreira, 746, Várzea;

Teresópolis, 3º Distrito: Rodovia Doutor Rogério de Moura Estevão, s/n, km 29, bairro Vale de Bonsucesso.

Com as cinco unidades, o Sicredi amplia sua presença física e aproxima o atendimento das diferentes realidades da Região Serrana. Além do acesso a produtos, serviços e orientação financeira, as agências disponibilizam aos associados salas para reuniões e treinamentos e espaços de coworking. Os locais também contam com profissionais preparados para compreender diferentes necessidades e apoiar a tomada de decisões financeiras.

O Sicredi é uma instituição financeira que em 2027 completará 125 anos de história, mais de 10,5 milhões de associados e presença em todo o Brasil. Com mais de 3,1 mil agências, oferece mais de 300 produtos e serviços financeiros para pessoas, empresas e o agronegócio, atuando com um modelo que valoriza o relacionamento próximo, a participação dos associados e o desenvolvimento das regiões onde está presente.

articles.title: TRE-RS: Locais de votação e alerta de fake news para o 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Justiça Eleitoral recomenda consulta ao e-Título, informa alterações pontuais em seções e lembra regras para transporte gratuito e votação.
articles.summary: O TRE-RS recomenda o uso do e-Título para conferir locais de votação e esclarece que apenas 12 seções sofreram alterações pontuais no segundo turno.
articles.body:
Boatos sobre mudanças em massa de locais de votação e outras informações falsas que circulam nas redes sociais levaram a Justiça Eleitoral a reforçar orientações aos eleitores para o segundo turno . No Rio Grande do Sul, segundo o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral (TRE), apenas 12 seções eleitorais tiveram alterações entre mais de 27 mil existentes no estado .

O alerta foi reforçado pelo secretário de Tecnologia da Informação do TRE-RS, Daniel Wobeto. Segundo ele, informações falsas sobre transferências generalizadas de seções eleitorais não condizem com a realidade .

"Houve muita divulgação de uma troca em massa das sessões para prejudicar o eleitor que absolutamente não condiz com a realidade. O trabalho dos cartórios eleitorais foi sempre voltado ao objetivo de facilitar a vida do eleitor", afirmou.

As alterações ocorreram em seções eleitorais dos municípios de Manoel Viana , Parobé , Santa Maria , São Luiz Gonzaga e Uruguaiana . A orientação é que os eleitores consultem previamente o local de votação para evitar transtornos .

Manoel Viana: a seção 62 funcionará na Escola Municipal de Ensino Fundamental Alberto Pasqualini.

Parobé: eleitoras e eleitores da seção 278 deverão comparecer ao Centro Municipal de Educação Ambiental João Marques de Souza (ESA).

Santa Maria: as seções 3 e 290 funcionarão na Escola Municipal de Ensino Infantil João Franciscatto.

São Luiz Gonzaga: seções 08, 81 e 118 na Escola Municipal de Ensino Fundamental José Bonifácio; seções 84 e 105 na Escola Municipal de Ensino Fundamental Ernestina Amaral Langsch.

Uruguaiana: as seções 97, 185 e 231 funcionarão na Escola Estadual de Ensino Fundamental República do Uruguai.

Para isso, a principal recomendação da Justiça Eleitoral é o uso do aplicativo e-Título . Conforme Wobeto, a ferramenta reúne as informações mais atualizadas sobre o cadastro eleitoral e o local onde o eleitor deve votar.

Além de indicar a zona, a seção e o endereço da votação, o aplicativo também pode ser usado para justificar a ausência por quem estiver fora do domicílio eleitoral.

Outra orientação é sobre o transporte gratuito. Haverá passe livre nos municípios por determinação do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral . A Trensurb também terá gratuidade no dia da eleição.

Já os eleitores que precisam viajar para outro município do Rio Grande do Sul poderão utilizar o transporte intermunicipal gratuito . Para isso, devem apresentar o título de eleitor e comprovar que votam na cidade de destino.

"Há a possibilidade dos eleitores se deslocarem mediante passagem gratuita das oito da manhã do sábado até as oito da manhã da segunda-feira, indo até a rodoviária apresentando o título de eleitor e demonstrando que é eleitor do outro município para poder receber a passagem gratuitamente", explicou.

A Justiça Eleitoral também lembra que quem não compareceu ao primeiro turno pode votar normalmente no segundo . Cada turno é considerado uma eleição independente para fins de comparecimento .

No dia da votação, o eleitor deve apresentar um documento oficial com foto ou o e-Título, se ele estiver com a foto do eleitor. O celular precisa permanecer com o mesário antes do ingresso na cabine de votação .

Para Wobeto, a participação eleitoral também representa um compromisso com a comunidade.

"A participação na eleição é um direito e um dever da pessoa, e eu acho que também é uma questão de dever comunitário. Se a pessoa faz parte de uma comunidade e aquela comunidade em geral não participa ela acaba perdendo relevância na sociedade. Então todos devem participar da eleição para dar o seu voto, para dar a sua opinião", afirmou.

articles.title: Teresópolis ganha relógio turístico na Praça Santa Teresa | G1
articles.standfirst: Inaugurado no dia da padroeira, equipamento com termômetro valoriza o espaço tradicional da cidade e oferece um novo serviço a moradores e visitantes.
articles.summary: Inaugurado no dia da padroeira, equipamento com termômetro valoriza o espaço tradicional da cidade e oferece um novo serviço a moradores e visitantes.
articles.body:
Novo relógio turístico da Praça Santa Teresa oferece informações de horário e temperatura a moradores e visitantes — Foto: Divulgação

Moradores e visitantes de Teresópolis agora contam com uma nova referência de horário e temperatura no Centro da cidade. A Praça Baltazar da Silveira, conhecida como Praça Santa Teresa, recebeu um relógio turístico com termômetro analógico, instalado próximo à Igreja Matriz. A inauguração ocorreu em 15 de outubro, dia de Santa Teresa d’Ávila, padroeira do município.

Idealizado pela Paróquia Santa Teresa d’Ávila, por meio do padre Jorge Luiz Pacheco de Medeiros, o projeto contou com a intermediação do Sincomércio de Teresópolis e o patrocínio do Sicredi. O equipamento reúne utilidade pública e valorização do espaço urbano, integrando-se a um dos principais pontos de convivência e circulação da cidade.

Uma parceria que aproxima instituições e pessoas

O projeto nasceu da aproximação entre a paróquia, a entidade representativa do comércio e a instituição financeira Sicredi, reunindo esforços para atender a uma demanda local. Essa articulação permite transformar propostas em benefícios para a população e reforça o compromisso das instituições com a valorização da cidade.

Tharles Brito, gerente da agência Sicredi Teresópolis, destaca que a participação dos associados torna possível apoiar iniciativas como essa. Presente em Teresópolis há cerca de dois anos e meio, a instituição reúne mais de três mil associados no município. “Quando fortalecemos os espaços públicos, valorizamos a cidade, movimentamos a economia local e criamos novas oportunidades para todos”, afirma Tharles.

Colaboradores do Sicredi e representante da Paróquia Santa Teresa d’Ávila durante a inauguração do relógio turístico na Praça Santa Teresa, em Teresópolis — Foto: Almanare

Uma entrega em uma data especial para Teresópolis

A inauguração do relógio integrou as celebrações da padroeira em um momento também marcado pela entrega das obras de restauração e ampliação da Igreja Matriz e de revitalização da Praça Santa Teresa.

O conjunto reforça a importância do local como espaço de convivência para famílias, moradores e turistas, preservando sua ligação com a história e a identidade de Teresópolis.

Para o Sicredi, apoiar o projeto representa uma forma de participar do cotidiano da cidade e contribuir para o desenvolvimento da região. Ao unir relacionamento próximo e apoio a iniciativas locais, a instituição fortalece sua conexão com as pessoas e com os espaços que fazem parte de suas histórias.

O apoio à instalação do relógio turístico faz parte de uma atuação mais ampla do Sicredi no município e em toda a Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro. Esse movimento ganha um novo capítulo no dia 26 de outubro, com a inauguração da agência do Vale de Bonsucesso, no Terceiro Distrito de Teresópolis. A nova unidade ampliará a presença física da instituição e o acesso a soluções financeiras para pessoas, empresas e produtores rurais.

A nova unidade aproxima o atendimento da realidade de quem vive, trabalha, empreende e produz na região. A expansão está alinhada ao posicionamento do Sicredi de ser parceiro para as conquistas das pessoas, dos negócios e da produção local, combinando atendimento humano, conhecimento das características de cada localidade e compromisso com o desenvolvimento dos territórios onde está presente.

O Sicredi é uma instituição financeira que em 2027 completará 125 anos de história, mais de 10,5 milhões de associados e presença em todo o Brasil. Com mais de 3,1 mil agências, oferece mais de 300 produtos e serviços financeiros para pessoas, empresas e o agronegócio, atuando com um modelo que valoriza o relacionamento próximo, a participação dos associados e o desenvolvimento das regiões onde está presente. articles.title: A Pennsylvania family was billed $1,800 for a car repair diagnosed under warranty; after repeated delays, the dealership admitted its mistake and cancelled the charge
articles.summary: Few things frustrate a vehicle owner more than a repair that was promised while coverage was active and then billed after it ended.
articles.body: Few things frustrate a vehicle owner more than a repair that was promised while coverage was active and then billed after it ended. A Pennsylvania family says that happened when a dealership took more than a year to replace a faulty air conditioning compressor, then asked them to pay $1,800 for work they believed the warranty should have covered. The dispute ended in the family's favour after the dealership reviewed its records and cancelled the charge. Here’s all that happened, how the family pushed back, what consumer warranty guidance says, and which records can protect you in future.How a faulty air conditioning compressor was diagnosed under warranty but never replaced for a yearAccording to a report by Guessing Headlights, a Pennsylvania husband described his family's experience in a July 3, 2026 post on the legal advice forum on Reddit. He wrote that his wife took the vehicle in for an inspection in June 2025 and reported that the air conditioning was not working properly. The dealership diagnosed a compressor problem while the vehicle was still under warranty, he said, but employees reportedly told her the replacement part was unavailable and had to be ordered. She was told the repair could be completed when she returned for an oil change about six weeks later. As the report notes, that replacement did not happen as promised, which set the dispute in motion.Missed promises, an unordered part and a lapsed warranty before the compressor was replaced in 2026When the woman returned for her oil change in August 2025, the dealership reportedly acknowledged it had never ordered the compressor. Employees again promised to get the part and contact her when it arrived, but, her husband said, they did not follow up before the warranty expired in October 2025. On July 2, 2026, she returned for another annual inspection, and this time the dealership finally had the compressor and replaced it. Her husband told Reddit readers that employees never explained the repair would no longer be covered and that no estimate was given for the $1,800 charge. When the dealership presented the bill, Guessing Headlights says it created a dispute over payment and over the release of the vehicle.How the family challenged the invoice and refused a reduced charge as the dealership checked recordsThe husband accused the dealership of deliberately delaying the work until the warranty ran out, although his account offers no independent evidence that the delays were intentional. After the family challenged the invoice, he said employees began reviewing earlier phone recordings and service records. The dealership offered to reduce the bill, but he maintained that his wife should owe nothing. He also alleged that employees suggested trading the vehicle toward a newer model while the billing dispute remained open. Commenters on the Reddit forum encouraged the family to gather documents showing when the compressor problem was first diagnosed, and others recommended escalating the complaint to the dealership's general manager or the vehicle manufacturer before immediately hiring an attorney.What consumer warranty guidance from the Federal Trade Commission says about defects reported earlyThe dispute highlights a distinction between when a mechanical problem is reported and when a dealership completes the repair. According to the Federal Trade Commission's consumer warranty guidance, a company must correct a covered defect reported during the warranty period if it was not properly resolved before coverage expired. The exact circumstances still matter, so vehicle owners should read their warranty agreements carefully. The commission also recommends contacting the manufacturer when a seller cannot resolve a warranty disagreement, and consumers can report unresolved problems to the commission or to their state attorney general. Because every warranty and every set of facts differs, anyone facing a similar bill may wish to check the agreement's wording or seek qualified advice.How the dealership cancelled the entire $1,800 charge and which records can help in similar disputesThe family ultimately got the outcome it wanted. In a July 9 update to the original discussion, the husband reported that the dealership acknowledged its mistake and eliminated the entire $1,800 charge. He explained that the dealership had kept message logs and recorded phone calls documenting earlier communications and promises about the repair, and he credited the business for correcting the situation instead of continuing to demand payment. The post did not name the dealership or the vehicle manufacturer, and the account has not been independently verified. Even so, the reported resolution shows why owners should keep repair orders, diagnostic reports, appointment confirmations and every message that documents the original complaint made while a vehicle was still under warranty.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A day after denying permission over \"specific threat-related inputs\" and security concerns, Delhi Police Friday cleared Diljit Dosanjh's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day after denying permission over "specific threat-related inputs" and security concerns, Delhi Police Friday cleared Diljit Dosanjh's concert, scheduled to be held at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on Oct 30.The nod came on a day when several Delhi schools received emails threatening that the singer's show would be targeted. A threat was received in Mumbai too, where he will perform on Nov 27.Police sources said the clearance was granted after organisers agreed to beef up arrangements for crowd management, deploy additional staff and coordinate with cops to ensure smooth conduct of the event.Cops advise organisers to coordinate with cab aggregatorsThe organisers have been asked to increase their staff by about 1,500 personnel to assist with various arrangements at the venue, including crowd regulation and the management of entry and exit points. Police have also stressed the need for better coordination between the organisers and security personnel to prevent congestion and ensure attendees can enter and leave the stadium with-out inconvenience.Sources said the organisers have been directed to inform concertgoers in advance about parking facilities, traffic arrangements and designated drop-off and pick-up points. They have also been asked to encourage attendees to use the metro to reduce the number of private vehicles travelling to the venue.Police have also advised the organisers to coordinate with cab aggregators to stream-line pick-up and drop-off arrangements and prevent traffic congestion around the stadium. They have also been asked to tie up with navigation platforms to keep attendees informed about designated routes and traffic diversions.In a statement, BookMyShow said reports suggesting that Dosanjh’s concert in Delhi had been cancelled were inaccurate.“Permission for the event had been temporarily withheld, not cancelled, pending additional safety, traffic and crowd-management measures requested by Delhi Police in view of the festive season. articles.summary: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing one person and injuring more than 500, while powerful winds and torrential rain brought down trees,
articles.body: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing one person and injuring more than 500, while powerful winds and torrential rain brought down trees, disrupted flights and knocked out electricity to thousands of homes.The storm has weakened and is heading north towards the Chinese coast, according to Reuters.Champi, which was previously classified as a super typhoon and was among the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, was packing gusts of around 126 kmph near its centre, Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA) said.The storm was about 150 km east of Taiwan on Saturday after passing close to the island's northeastern coast in the early hours. Its forecast track showed it turning north towards the Chinese coast before eventually moving towards southern Japan.One dead, over 500 injured as strong winds batter TaiwanTaiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at one, after a man was swept away by waves on Liuqiu Island. A further 527 people were injured amid strong winds and heavy rainfall.Visuals from Taiwan showed gargantuan waves crashing ashore as the typhoon approached.Other footage captured a woman struggling against powerful gusts, while strong winds continued to affect parts of the island.The storm also caused widespread power disruptions. Taipower, Taiwan's state-owned electricity company, said more than 167,000 homes had lost electricity at one point, although power had been restored to most affected households.Transport services were also disrupted, with the transport ministry reporting 242 flight cancellations on Saturday. The figure was significantly lower than Friday, when cancellations had approached 1,000.In Taipei, the island's capital, trees were brought down by the winds, while intermittent squally rain showers continued.Authorities in parts of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, extended office and school closures for a second day on Saturday.Taiwan braces for storm's impact as it moves northTaiwan had largely shut down on Friday as Champi approached, with schools, offices and financial markets closing and hundreds of flights grounded. Authorities had also evacuated more than 2,600 people from vulnerable mountainous areas.The CWA had warned that the storm's large wind radius could expose much of Taiwan to strong winds for an extended period. Forecaster Liu Pei-teng told Reuters on Friday that a direct landfall could not be ruled out if the storm changed direction or slowed down near the island.“The storm's wind radius is quite large, among the bigger ones in recent years,” Liu said. “If the storm slows down, the strong winds will affect Taiwan for longer.”The storm had earlier reached maximum sustained winds of 298 kmph before weakening as it approached Taiwan, according to the news agency Associated Press.Its centre was forecast to remain offshore as it passed the island's northeastern tip and turned towards Japan's southwestern islands.Taiwan is generally well prepared for typhoons, which helps keep casualties low. Although such storms are more common during summer, they can also strike in autumn.Champi's forecast path now takes it north towards the Chinese coast, with the storm expected to eventually move towards southern Japan.You use AI every day. articles.body: Selena Gomez hosted her fourth annual Rare Impact Fund Benefit in Los Angeles on Wednesday, 14 October. The evening combined fundraising for youth mental health non-profits with a few lighter moments, including a visible show of support from her husband, Benny Blanco.Blanco bid $25,000 at the event’s live auction to win a session titled “Session with Selena Gomez’s Official ‘Glam Team’”, which includes hairstylist Renato Campora, make-up artist Jenna Nicole and nail artist Tom Bachik.Benny Blanco continues to be Selena Gomez’s No. 1 supporterMusic producer Benny Blanco, 38, has always been Selena Gomez’s biggest cheerleader. So, at the benefit, he made sure he showed his support. The live auction produced the night’s most talked-about bid. Blanco raised his paddle several times before winning a package listed as a session with Gomez’s official glam team. The experience includes a styling session with hairstylist Renato Campora, a make-up session with artist Jenna Nicole and a custom nail look by Tom Bachik, according to the Rare Impact Fund Benefit auction page. Blanco’s final bid was $25,000. Gomez, 34, was seen leaning on him as the bidding closed. The couple tied the knot on 27 September 2025.The gala raised $2.7 million through sponsors, donors and the live auction combined, a press release confirms. The 2024 benefit raised more than $2 million, according to Billboard, so this year’s figure represents a step up.Selena Gomez’s mission to improve youth mental healthSelena Gomez launched the Rare Impact Fund in 2020, and 1 per cent of all Rare Beauty sales is donated to it. The initiative is part of her commitment to “addressing mental health and self-acceptance”.“Mental health is personal for me. I went a long time without the support I needed because I didn’t understand what I was feeling. But I’m learning every day that supporting my mental health is a journey. Every day isn’t perfect, not for me, not for anyone. articles.title: India highlights nuclear advances, development partnerships at UNGA session
articles.summary: India has reaffirmed its commitment to the safe, secure and peaceful uses of nuclear science and technology at the 81st session of the United Nations
articles.body: India has reaffirmed its commitment to the safe, secure and peaceful uses of nuclear science and technology at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), highlighting the role of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in promoting sustainable development and strengthening institutional capabilities.Sangeeta Kumari Singh Deo, Member of Parliament and leader of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation, addressed the General Assembly on the report of the IAEA, underlining the agency's role in helping member states develop human and institutional capacities, including regulatory frameworks for the peaceful application of nuclear science.In a post on X, India's mission to the UN said Singh Deo highlighted India's advancements in nuclear technology and its support for the IAEA's Technical Cooperation Programme and flagship initiatives.The mission also said India had reiterated its commitment to South-South cooperation to ensure that the benefits of nuclear science reach countries seeking them, while maintaining robust nuclear safety and security frameworks.Countries thank India for development assistanceSeparately, several countries acknowledged India's development assistance at the Ninth Annual India-UN Development Partnership Fund event held on October 22.Representatives from Laos, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Micronesia, Moldova, Morocco and Saint Lucia were among those expressing appreciation for India's support.Moldova's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Gheorghe Leuca, said the partnership had strengthened the country's ability to use population data to improve public policies.“At a time of ODA strain, India's sustained committment sends an important message: ‘Partnership built on solidarity, mutual respect and national priorities can continue to deliver tangible results,’” Leuca said.Sri Lanka's UN envoy, ambassador Jayantha Jayasuriya, said the India-UN Fund addressed diverse thematic areas and supported projects based on the needs identified by participating countries.“The India-UN Fund caters to diversified thematic structures and these projects respond to needs identified by the countries themselves... its underlying philosophy is that respect for national priorities matters,” he said.Laos' UN ambassador, Thongphane Savanphet, commended India's role in advancing cooperation among developing countries.“We commend the Govt of India for the vital role in promoting the South-South cooperation. The India-UN Fund serves as an example of solidarity and partnership among developing countries, in supporting national development priorities. India has also extended its general support for our national priorities through other cooperation mechanisms,” he said.Tanzania's representative to the UN, ambassador Togolani Edriss Mavura, also expressed appreciation for India's continued support for sustainable development in the country.“Tanzania expresses its sincere appreciation to India and the India-UN Fund for their continued support for sustainable development in Tanzania,” he said.A representative of Morocco's delegation praised India's role in the initiative, saying: “We commend India's vision and generosity, as well as the UN Office of South-South Cooperation for its dedicated stewardship of this demand-driven initiative. Nearly a decade after its launch in 2017, the fund's record speaks for itself.”Mozambique's Permanent Representative to the UN, ambassador Domingos Estêvão Fernandes, said the fund demonstrated South-South cooperation based on national priorities, equality and non-interference, while complementing North-South cooperation.IAEA highlights growing role of nuclear energyMeanwhile, IAEA director-general Rafael Grossi told the UN General Assembly that global nuclear power use could more than triple by 2060.Grossi said the projected growth would be driven by electrification, data centres powered by artificial intelligence and technology companies' demand for reliable, carbon-free electricity.“In 2025, more than 400 operating reactors in more than 30 countries produced 10 per cent of global electricity and a quarter of its low-carbon electricity,” Grossi said. He added that more than 60 new reactors were under construction and projections for future nuclear capacity had increased significantly.Grossi also addressed nuclear programmes in Iran and North Korea, threats to nuclear safety linked to the war in Ukraine, and progress in clarifying questions about Syria's nuclear activities.On Iran, he called for renewed diplomatic efforts and said IAEA inspectors needed to return to the country to support verification under any sustainable agreement.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 7 Days, 7 Chakras, 7 Heavens: Why Does the Number 7 Keep Appearing in Spiritual Traditions?
articles.summary: At a Hindu wedding, the bride and groom take seven steps around the sacred fire. In Mecca, pilgrims circle the Kaaba seven times.
articles.body: At a Hindu wedding, the bride and groom take seven steps around the sacred fire. In Mecca, pilgrims circle the Kaaba seven times. The Bible describes creation in seven days. Music in India rests on seven notes, from Sa to Ni. People raised in very different worlds keep landing on the same number. That pattern has fascinated scholars and spiritual seekers for centuries. Why seven?Seven Begins in the SkyThe simplest answer may be overhead. Ancient observers, without telescopes, could see seven moving lights against the fixed stars. These were the Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.Those seven bodies gave the week its shape. Sunday belongs to the Sun, Monday to the Moon, and so on through Saturday, named for Saturn. Indian weekday names follow the same pattern. Ravivar for Ravi, the Sun. Somvar for Soma, the Moon. Shanivar for Shani. Two cultures far apart built their calendars on the same seven lights.The Moon added support. Its main phases, from New Moon to First Quarter to Full Moon, come roughly seven days apart. So seven became a natural unit of time.The night sky offered one more seven. The Saptarishi, the seven great sages of Hindu tradition, are linked with the seven bright stars that many know as the Big Dipper.Seven in Indian TraditionHindu ritual is full of sevens. The best known is Saptapadi, the seven steps at the heart of a Hindu marriage. Each step carries a vow about food, strength, prosperity, family and lifelong friendship. A marriage is considered complete only after the seventh step.The Sun god Surya rides a chariot pulled by seven horses. Many read these as the seven colours of sunlight. Scriptures describe seven upper worlds, or lokas, and seven lower ones.The Rig Veda speaks of Sapta Sindhu, the land of seven rivers, often taken as an early name for northwest India. And yoga traditions describe seven main chakras, energy centres running from the base of the spine to the crown of the head.Music follows the same rule. The seven swaras of Indian classical music form the base of every raga.Seven in Other FaithsIn the Bible, God creates the world in six days and rests on the seventh. That rest day, the Sabbath, made seven a symbol of completion and holiness. Seven appears again and again in the Book of Revelation, with seven seals and seven churches.Islam describes seven heavens. During Hajj and Umrah, pilgrims perform tawaf, circling the Kaaba seven times. They also walk seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah.Buddhist tradition tells that the newborn Buddha took seven steps, with lotuses blooming beneath his feet. In Japan, the Seven Lucky Gods are popular symbols of good fortune.Even science added a seven by choice. Isaac Newton divided the rainbow into seven colours, partly because he wanted it to match the seven notes of a musical scale.Seven in NumerologyGiven all this, it isn’t surprising that numerology treats seven as a spiritual number. In Western numerology, 7 is the seeker, the person drawn to understand what lies beneath surface events.Indian numerology assigns 7 to Ketu, the south lunar node. Ketu stands for detachment and moksha, release from worldly ties. Cheiro’s Chaldean system linked 7 with Neptune, the planet of mysticism and dreams.People strongly influenced by 7 often feel pulled toward meditation, research or quiet reflection. Many need time alone more than most people do. That solitude isn’t loneliness. For them, it’s how insight arrives.Seven also shows up as a measure of completion in everyday spiritual practice. Many people chant a mantra seven times, or keep a fast for seven Mondays. The idea is the same everywhere. Seven marks a full cycle, after which something new can begin.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Psychology says people who always arrive early may have a distinct way of dealing with uncertainty; what punctuality reveals about control, responsibility and stress
articles.summary: There is always someone who reaches the airport hours before departure, arrives at a restaurant before the rest of the group or leaves home early enough
articles.body: There is always someone who reaches the airport hours before departure, arrives at a restaurant before the rest of the group or leaves home early enough to account for traffic, parking and an unexpected delay. While others are watching the clock, this person is already there, waiting.It is easy to describe such people as disciplined and organised. But arriving early can also reflect how a person approaches uncertainty, responsibility and the need to feel prepared. The reasons, however, are not the same for everyone. For some, punctuality is simply a useful habit; for others, it may help ease the discomfort of not knowing what could go wrong.Early arrival may reflect conscientiousnessOne psychological explanation for punctuality is conscientiousness, a personality trait associated with organisation, dependability and self-discipline.A 2006 study published in the Journal of Research in Personality examined the relationship between the Big Five personality traits and punctuality. Researchers Mitja D. Back, Stefan C. Schmukle and Boris Egloff studied 92 participants who completed personality questionnaires before attending a scheduled psychological experiment.The researchers recorded participants’ arrival times, including how early or late they were. They found that conscientiousness was associated with all three measures of punctuality. Agreeableness was also related to arrival time and earliness, while neuroticism was associated with earliness.The findings suggest that punctuality can be part of a broader pattern of behaviour. People who plan ahead, prepare for appointments and allow time for unexpected problems may be applying the same organisational habits they use elsewhere.However, this was a small study involving university students. It does not mean that every early arriver has the same personality or that arriving early automatically makes someone more responsible.Arriving early may help people manage uncertaintyImagine two people travelling to an important meeting. One checks the estimated journey time and leaves accordingly. The other adds another 30 minutes because traffic might be worse, parking could be difficult or the venue might be hard to find.Both are planning ahead. But the second person may also be seeking reassurance that an unexpected problem will not make them late.Psychologists use the term intolerance of uncertainty to describe difficulty dealing with unpredictable situations or incomplete information. Research has linked this tendency to worry and anxiety.A useful starting point is the research literature on intolerance of uncertainty and anxiety, which examines how uncertainty can contribute to worry and anxious responses.This research does not establish that people who arrive early have a higher intolerance of uncertainty. It does, however, offer a possible explanation for why some people prefer to build large time buffers into their plans.If uncertainty feels uncomfortable, leaving early can make a situation feel more manageable. A person cannot guarantee that traffic will move smoothly, but they can reduce the chances of a delay making them late.The important distinction is whether the extra time provides convenience or becomes necessary for emotional reassurance. Someone who arrives early and relaxes while waiting may simply be organised. Someone who remains anxious until every possible obstacle has been accounted for may be using the habit to manage worry.Punctuality can create a sense of controlPeople cannot control every part of their day. Trains can be delayed, meetings can run over time and traffic can change without warning. But they can decide when to leave, prepare in advance and allow room for setbacks.Planning can therefore create a sense of control, even when circumstances remain unpredictable.A 2021 meta-analysis published in PLOS ONE by Brad Aeon, Aïda Faber and Alexandra Panaccio examined 158 studies involving 53,957 participants. The researchers assessed the relationship between time management, performance and well-being.They found that time management was moderately associated with job performance, academic achievement and well-being. It also showed a moderate negative relationship with distress.These findings suggest that managing time effectively can be useful beyond simply reaching places on schedule. Planning and organising activities may help people feel more prepared and manage competing demands.For early arrivers, this could mean that leaving a buffer reduces the pressure of rushing. Instead of reacting to every obstacle as it occurs, they have already allowed for some of it.However, planning has limits. A flexible person can adapt when circumstances change. If a small delay causes disproportionate distress, the desire to stay in control may be creating pressure rather than relieving it.The difference lies in whether planning helps a person handle uncertainty or whether they feel compelled to eliminate it altogether.Being early may reflect responsibility towards othersPunctuality is also a social behaviour. Arriving early for a job interview, reaching an office meeting before it begins or leaving home on time for a family appointment may reflect a desire not to inconvenience others.People often interpret punctuality as a sign of reliability, particularly in professional settings. Research on reactions to lateness offers some insight into why.A person's reason for arriving late can influence how others judge them. When lateness appears avoidable, it may be interpreted differently from a delay caused by circumstances beyond someone's control.This means that early arrival can serve a practical social purpose: it reduces the risk of keeping others waiting and helps a person meet an agreed commitment.Yet responsibility does not require arriving excessively early for every occasion. Reaching someone's home well before the agreed time, for example, may inconvenience a host who is still preparing.Punctuality is most useful when it respects both the commitment and the people involved.When does punctuality become a source of stress?The same behaviour can have very different emotional effects.One person may arrive 15 minutes early to settle down, have a coffee or review their notes. Another may spend those 15 minutes repeatedly checking the time and worrying about what might have happened if they had encountered a delay.The outward behaviour is identical, but the experience is not.The 2006 study on personality and punctuality found an association between neuroticism and earliness. Neuroticism refers to a tendency to experience negative emotions; the finding does not prove that early arrivals are generally anxious.It is equally important not to assume that people who arrive late are careless or relaxed. Punctuality can be shaped by personality, habits, competing responsibilities and circumstances.A useful question is whether the habit remains flexible. Can someone who usually leaves early adjust their plans without becoming distressed? Can they accept that a delay is sometimes unavoidable?If so, early arrival may simply be an effective routine. If the possibility of being late creates intense worry or guilt, it may be worth examining the expectations behind that reaction.What arriving early may reveal about youThere is no single psychological explanation for people who consistently arrive early. Their behaviour may reflect conscientiousness, consideration for others, a preference for predictability or several factors at once.Rather than treating punctuality as a personality test, it may help to ask three questions:Does arriving early help me feel prepared? If it gives you time to settle in and focus, it may be a useful habit.Am I trying to avoid inconveniencing others? If so, punctuality may reflect consideration and responsibility.Can I cope when plans change? If a small delay causes disproportionate worry, it may be worth exploring why uncertainty feels uncomfortable.Ultimately, arriving early does not automatically indicate anxiety, a need for control or exceptional discipline. The behaviour alone cannot reveal the full story.The more revealing distinction is between someone who arrives early because they have made room for life's unpredictability and someone who feels they must anticipate every possible problem before they can relax.One uses time as a practical resource. articles.summary: Sooryavanshi remains in strong contention to feature in India's playing XI as a top-order batter following the adductor injury to Ishan Kishan.
articles.body:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may finally get a chance in India's playing XI for the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch.

The teenager has been left out of six consecutive T20 internationals, and he also sat out the series opener on Thursday, which India won to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

The door has now opened because of an injury to Ishan Kishan, who has been ruled out of this game with a groin strain. Kishan's absence leaves a vacancy in the batting order, and Sooryavanshi is the most obvious replacement, particularly given his explosive strike rate.

Many fans have wanted to see him in action for weeks, and this looks like the cleanest way for the team management to give him a game without dropping a settled opener.

Will Vaibhav Sooryavanshi play today in the 2nd T20I at Hagley Oval, Christchurch?

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi should get a chance to open the innings in the 2nd T20I.

There is, however, one catch. The management is understood to be considering Varun Chakravarthy as an alternative, which would mean going for extra bowling instead of a like-for-like batting change. India's bowlers conceded 225 in the first match, so the idea of strengthening that department is not hard to understand.

Should Chakravarthy be preferred, Sooryavanshi's wait for a game will stretch even further, and the debate over his limited opportunities will only grow louder. The final decision is expected when the team sheets are announced at the toss.
